items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: taking classical music à la Mozart, à la Haydn, à la Pergolesi, à la Bach

ctx.x: Oh yeah. So I did all this composing. At first, because the – a lot of people aren’t going to like hearing this – the music world in the United States, and certainly in New York, was completely controlled in the mid-1940s into the early 1950s by a style of music we call neo-classic. That was the music basically of Stravinsky and of Aaron Copland. Stravinsky had written the greatest masterpiece of the twentieth century, I believe, which is called the Sacre du printemps – The Rite of Spring. He wrote that in 1913.…
